assessments.reasoning: Oracle gives LOCAL and arguments as alternatives that make a procedure local and describes ordinary variables as local. The next physical page expressly permits declaring global variables inside a local procedure by adding an underscore after the variable marker. The frozen second sentence encompasses these explicitly global declarations, and its limitation only describes access to globals.

challenge.method: Read the complete BEGIN-PROCEDURE description across physical pages 60–61, including default global procedures, declarations with arguments, shadowing, and the explicit global-variable syntax within local procedures.
challenge.results: The locality trigger is explicit. The blanket second sentence fails because Oracle says the underscore form can declare global variables from within a local procedure, not only access them. Hold this revision and verify a new revision that limits the rule to local declarations or explicitly excludes the underscore form.

limitations: The same section separately documents access to global variables from within a local procedure through a leading underscore after the variable marker.
The frozen limitation names access to globals but does not exclude global declarations within local procedures.
